task: Provision default LiteLLM customers and user_budget_assignments rows per configured predefined budget at user creation (registration, admin create, IdP first login, dev header), fail-open, instead of lazily on first LLM request.

key_reasoning.reason: Four hook sites across RegistrationService, UserManagementService and AuthenticationService, plus a new BudgetService method and a changed provider contract (protocol, noop, LiteLLM adapter). All within the service layer of one repo and built from reusable pieces (build_user_id, resolve_mirrored_budget_id, upsert_user_category_assignment, _record_default_assignment pattern).

Closest pattern is the existing fail-open post-commit hooks (provision_global_user, _sync_budget_for_idp_projects) and _record_default_assignment. It does not cover the sync/async seams (async method with sync session, asyncio.run, async IdP and dev-header paths), the login-path latency of 1-3 blocking LiteLLM calls per category, or the None-return failure signal (a row written after a failed customer create would persist a wrong budget that lazy and backfill paths never correct). The per-process assignment cache and the shared provider protocol change add to the risk. Auth-adjacent but no authz change.

About 7-8 source files modified (registration_service, user_management_service, authentication_service, budget_service, provider protocol, provider_registry noop, budget_provider_adapter, possibly a gate helper), plus about 5-6 existing test files updated and 1-2 new test files. Three to four directories (service/user, service/budget, enterprise/litellm, tests).

red_flags_applied: Affects multiple workflows: Component Scope held at L (4), not bumped further, since all call sites share one new BudgetService entry point
Clarity: the task's path 3 (IntegrityError recovery distinction) and path 4 (post-commit point is outside the if-block) are contradicted by the code, so Requirements Clarity sits at M
